Scores and bread for the sandwich package

Source: R/vcov_cluster.R
estfun.flexCountReg.Rd

Methods that make flexCountReg fits work with sandwich::vcovCL(), sandwich::vcovHC(), sandwich::sandwich() and, through them, lmtest::coeftest() and modelsummary(vcov = ~ cluster).

Usage

# S3 method for class 'flexCountReg'
estfun(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'flexCountReg'
bread(x, ...)

Arguments

x

a fitted flexCountReg model.

...

not used.

Value

estfun(): a matrix with one row per unit and one column per parameter. bread(): a square matrix.

Details

estfun() returns the scores of the model's independent units: one row per row of the data used in estimation, or per panel for panel models, multiplied by the weights. bread() is \(n (-H)^{-1}\) with \(n\) the number of units, the convention of the sandwich package, so sandwich::sandwich(m) is \((-H)^{-1} \sum_i s_i s_i' (-H)^{-1}\).

The sandwich package treats each row of estfun() as an independent unit. That is right without weights and for sampling weights; with frequency weights, use vcov(m, type = "robust") or type = "cluster", which count a row with weight \(w\) as \(w\) observations. For panel models, a cluster variable for vcovCL() must have one value per panel (in the order of the panel ids); vcov(m, type = "cluster", cluster = ~ v) takes the variable from the data.

Examples

# \donttest{
data("washington_roads")
m <- countreg(Total_crashes ~ lnaadt + lnlength, data = washington_roads,
              family = "NB2", method = "BFGS")
sandwich::vcovCL(m, cluster = washington_roads$ID, type = "HC0")
#>              (Intercept)        lnaadt      lnlength    ln(alpha)
#> (Intercept)  0.343855393 -3.923457e-02  7.031254e-03  0.022182837
#> lnaadt      -0.039234573  4.610843e-03  3.194782e-05 -0.002843661
#> lnlength     0.007031254  3.194782e-05  7.591455e-03 -0.001220079
#> ln(alpha)    0.022182837 -2.843661e-03 -1.220079e-03  0.058516309
# }
